text:
maya (pm): Heads-up: Sales + customers keep asking for a clear plan on isolation tiers, pricing delta, and cutover safety. We need a crisp decision doc by Friday that ties launch gates to measurable signals.

olivia (sales): FinCorp wants guaranteed latency and a hard isolation lane. They'll pay for reserved capacity but need a predictable monthly invoice + overage policy. Healthly wants private deploy option and audit logs.

linh (eng-plat): Proposing three isolation tiers for the product page: shared (best-effort), reserved (committed pool), private (VPC/on-prem). Each tier needs concrete SLOs and cost multipliers.

rachel (eng-ml): From model side, reserved and private lanes simplify kernel selection and quantization constraints. But we must publish model-compatibility matrix: some quantized variants are incompatible with our fastest kernels.

maya (pm): Important: For the decision doc, include these launch gates per tier:
- shared: routing policy API + soft-affinity fallback + cross-region spill detection
- reserved: capacity commit or guaranteed pool with warm-start ramp + billing enforcement + canary with 2 paying customers
- private: private control plane + KMS integration + compliance checklist + partner install runbook

tom (infra): Implementation notes: reserved lanes can be done two ways: 1) tenant-dedicated pools (full isolation), 2) reservation tagging on a shared pool with strict eviction. Option 1 is simpler for guarantees but costs more and needs capacity commits. Option 2 is cheaper but complex (eviction semantics, noisy neighbour mitigation).

anika (sre): Operationally we need: chaos suite for eviction scenarios, synthetic load tests to measure tail latency under spill, and alerting on cross-region egress growth (threshold rule). Also a playbook for forced-eviction rollback.

olivia (sales): We should offer a migration credit for early adopters who sign reserved lanes to help them accept capacity commit. Sales will table the credit as negotiating tool.

linh (eng-plat): API sketch for routing policy CLI: 
```
redwood policy create --tenant fincorp \
  --preferred-regions eu-west-1,us-east-1 \
  --isolation reserved --capacity-gb 512 --fallback nearest
```
Console needs a visual indicator for lane costs and expected latency.

rachel (eng-ml): Also include a quality monitoring gate: when fallback to smaller or different model variant happens, we run a prompt set and ensure BLEU/ROUGE/QA pass-rate delta < X%. If not, auto-rollback or throttle fallback.

maya (pm): Acceptance metrics we can publish: 
- shared: p95 < 150ms normally, p99 < 450ms under 95th percentile load
- reserved: p95 < 120ms, p99 < 300ms
- private: capable of meeting customer's contractual SLO (documented per-deal)
Also: fallback quality delta < 3% on eval prompts, and billing enforcement triggered within 1 minute of quota breach.

tom (infra): Bandwidth and egress: we must cap cross-region replication during spill and apply backpressure, otherwise costs explode. Capacity-bot will help simulate costs during canary.

capacity-bot: Simulation run started for reserved-lane cost model with 3 demand profiles at 1799012360. Results will post in ~10m.

anika (sre): For the cutover plan: stage 1 = enable soft-affinity + telemetry; stage 2 = enable per-tenant reservations in a staging pool; stage 3 = allocate dedicated pools for canary tenants; stage 4 = if canary OK, push to prod with 24h warm-up window. Each stage must have abort criteria (error rate, SLO regressions, cost deltas).

olivia (sales): Can we get a simple one-pager that maps price delta vs expected percent decrease in noisy-neighbor incidents? Sales needs that to discuss the value prop.

rachel (eng-ml): We'll provide a short appendix with model perf delta across quantization settings and kernels. That will feed the price-vs-performance one-pager.

linh (eng-plat): Dependencies: research (compat matrix), runtime (kernel gating + warm-start APIs), infra (pool allocation + egress caps), billing (quota + overage rate), console (policy UI). Need to add delivery owners in the doc.

maya (pm): Owners assigned in the decision doc draft: Linh (policy API), Tom (infra pools), Rachel (compat matrix), Anika (SRE tests), Olivia (sales pilot coord). I'll draft PR and ping legal/finance for billing wording.

anika (sre): I'll start a red-team runbook that intentionally evicts a canary tenant and measures user-facing errors and degradation metrics. We should schedule this with the canary tenants.

capacity-bot: Cost sim complete for profile B: reserved-lane monthly base + 20% peak buffer results in +2.3x cost vs shared but reduces spill incidents by ~78% in sim. Report posted to /shared/cost-sims/1799012345.

maya (pm): Good. Next steps: I'll produce the decision doc with the gates + one-pager and assign a review deadline (Thu end of day). Please add any missing risks.

tom (infra): Risk: cold-start on dedicated pools may increase token latency for bursty tenants unless we keep a warm buffer. That needs to be baked into pricing.

olivia (sales): Risk noted  we'll include a recommended warm-buffer SKU.

maya (pm): Thanks everyone. If no objections I'll turn this thread into the PR and include the canary schedule.

anika (sre): No objections from me. Will coordinate chaos dates.

linh (eng-plat): One more ask: add a telemetry event for "policy-fallback" with context (tenant, fallback_model, latency, region) so quality & billing can correlate.

maya (pm): Added to the doc. PR incoming.
